questions.scenario: Your school is hosting a massive carnival, and you have Rs. 1000 to spend. What is your strategy?

options.text: I give it to a friend starting a risky but totally unique game stall, in exchange for 50% of their profits.
I convince two small food stalls to merge together so they can defeat the biggest stall, taking a fee for my advice.
I spread the money evenly across 5 different games and food stalls so I don't lose it all on one bad choice.
I analyze the foot traffic and past year's data to mathematically calculate which stall will definitely make the most money.

questions.scenario: You are playing a strategy video game or a fantasy sports league. What is your playstyle?

options.text: I draft unknown, low-level 'rookie' characters hoping they suddenly become super powerful later.
I constantly trade players/items with other gamers to build the most expensive, star-studded team.
I build a perfectly balanced team with solid defense and offense to guarantee consistent points every week.
I use advanced spreadsheets and min-max all my stats to find the exact mathematical way to win.

questions.scenario: You are trying to buy a new phone or gadget. How do you approach the purchase?

options.text: I buy from a brand-new startup company because their wild new tech looks like the future.
I buy a popular phone but negotiate aggressively at the shop to get free accessories and the best exchange deal.
I buy a reliable, mid-range phone from a trusted brand that will definitely last me 4 years without issues.
I compare the exact processor speeds, battery benchmarks, and price-to-performance ratios before buying.

questions.scenario: Your friend group is trying to decide what movie to watch, and everyone is arguing. What do you do?

options.text: I hype up a completely unknown indie movie because I have a gut feeling it's going to be a masterpiece.
I act as the middleman, negotiating between the action-lovers and comedy-lovers until a deal is made.
I suggest a theater that has an arcade and a food court, so no matter what movie we pick, everyone is happy.
I look up IMDb ratings, Rotten Tomatoes scores, and runtimes to pick the statistically best movie.

questions.scenario: When you watch YouTube or scroll social media, what excites you the most?

options.text: Finding a channel with only 100 subscribers that is doing something totally new, before they go viral.
Watching videos about huge corporate dramas, billionaires, and massive company buyouts.
Subscribing to a safe mix of education, gaming, comedy, and news so my feed is perfectly balanced.
Analyzing a creator's views-to-likes ratio to see if their growth is actually real or just clickbait.

questions.scenario: How do you prefer to handle your pocket money or savings?

options.text: I use it to fund my friend's idea to start a small custom t-shirt hustle at school.
I use it to buy rare sneakers or game skins, wait a bit, and flip them to someone else for a fast profit.
I put a fixed amount into a bank account every single month so my savings grow steadily over time.
I create an Excel sheet tracking every single rupee I spend to completely optimize my budget.

questions.scenario: Your teacher announces a huge group project. How do you prepare to get the best grade?

options.text: I choose a really out-of-the-box, risky topic that the teacher has never seen before.
I convince the smartest kids from different friend groups to merge and form one 'super group' with me.
I make sure our project covers a little bit of everything the rubric asks for, minimizing the chance of losing points.
I look at 5 years of past projects to calculate exactly what formatting and words get the highest marks.

questions.scenario: If you were collecting items (like Pokémon cards, sneakers, or comic books), what is your style?

options.text: Buying cards of brand-new characters hoping they become super famous and valuable in 10 years.
Buying whole collections in bulk and instantly selling the individual items to other collectors for a markup.
Keeping a diverse collection of different types of cards so the overall value of my folder never crashes.
Tracking the daily online price charts of individual cards to know the exact mathematical moment to sell.

questions.scenario: What is the worst feeling for you?

options.text: Missing out on being the 'first' to discover a cool trend or idea before everyone else.
Losing an argument or failing to close a deal that I was negotiating.
Taking a huge, unnecessary risk and losing everything because of it.
Making a decision based purely on emotion instead of logic and data.

questions.scenario: What sounds like the ultimate career achievement to you?

options.text: Being the person who funded the next Google, Tesla, or world-changing invention when it was just an idea.
Being the ultimate deal-maker, sitting in high-stakes boardrooms finalizing billion-dollar company mergers.
Safely and steadily growing massive amounts of wealth over decades for myself and my clients.
Building the smartest, most complex mathematical AI models that can predict the future of the stock market.

Venture_Capitalist.title: Venture Capitalist / Angel Investor
Venture_Capitalist.primary_match_text: You are a visionary risk-taker. You don't want to follow the crowd; you want to spot the next big thing before anyone else does.
Venture_Capitalist.day_in_the_life: Meeting young startup founders, listening to their crazy new ideas, and deciding whether to give them millions of dollars to build their company.
Venture_Capitalist.alternative_match_text: Because you love finding hidden potential and taking calculated risks, investing in early-stage startups is the perfect high-reward career for you.
Venture_Capitalist.roadmap: Take Commerce or Science in 11th/12th. Pursue a BBA, B.Com, or B.Tech, followed by a top-tier MBA. Start networking in startup ecosystems early.

Investment_Banker.title: Investment Banker / M&A Specialist
Investment_Banker.primary_match_text: You are the ultimate deal-maker. You love high-stakes negotiations, connecting people, and being in the center of the action.
Investment_Banker.day_in_the_life: Advising massive corporations, helping companies buy out their rivals (Mergers & Acquisitions), and raising billions of dollars for giant projects.
Investment_Banker.alternative_match_text: Since you thrive in high-pressure situations and love negotiating, helping massive companies make billion-dollar deals is your natural playground.
Investment_Banker.roadmap: Take Commerce (with Math) in 11th/12th. Pursue B.Com (Hons), Economics, or BBA, followed by a highly ranked MBA in Finance or a CFA certification.

Portfolio_Manager.title: Portfolio Manager / Wealth Manager
Portfolio_Manager.primary_match_text: You are strategic, patient, and risk-averse. You know that slow and steady wins the race, and you prefer perfectly balanced plans over wild gambles.
Portfolio_Manager.day_in_the_life: Managing millions of dollars for clients or mutual funds, carefully deciding how much money goes into safe stocks, gold, or real estate so they never lose their wealth.
Portfolio_Manager.alternative_match_text: Because you are great at balancing risks and planning for the long term, managing massive wealth portfolios is a highly lucrative and stable path.
Portfolio_Manager.roadmap: Take Commerce in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Com or BBA. Completing your CFA (Chartered Financial Analyst) or CA is highly recommended for this role.

Quant_Analyst.title: Quantitative Analyst (Quant)
Quant_Analyst.primary_match_text: You are a math and logic wizard. You don't trust emotions or gut feelings—you trust raw data, algorithms, and complex statistics.
Quant_Analyst.day_in_the_life: Writing complex Python or C++ code and building AI models that can analyze the stock market faster than humanly possible to make split-second trades.
Quant_Analyst.alternative_match_text: If you love breaking down complex systems using math and code, becoming a 'Quant' is one of the highest-paying and most elite jobs in finance.
Quant_Analyst.roadmap: Take Science (PCM) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Tech (Computer Science/Math) or B.Sc in Statistics, followed by a Master's in Financial Engineering or Data Science.
